sq.QUESTION_DESC: In a warehouse, boxes are arranged in places where their size is fixed. Mr.Tilak store incharge wants to insert the box in the middle and he visits all the boxes one by one from starting to ending. Write the appropriate pseudo code for the above mentioned concept

sq.ANSWER:
Deletion at the Beginning

PROCEDURE DeleteAtBeginning(head)

    IF head IS NULL THEN

        PRINT "List is empty"

        RETURN NULL

    END IF

 

    SET temp = head

    SET head = head.next

    DELETE temp

 

    RETURN head

END PROCEDURE

AFTER DELETION: HEAD → [102, "Bob"] → [103, "Charlie"] → NULL

 

Deletion at the End

PROCEDURE DeleteAtEnd(head)

    IF head IS NULL THEN

        PRINT "List is empty"

        RETURN NULL

    END IF

 

    IF head.next IS NULL THEN

        DELETE head

        RETURN NULL

    END IF

 

    SET current = head

    WHILE current.next.next IS NOT NULL DO

        SET current = current.next

    END WHILE

 

    DELETE current.next

    SET current.next = NULL

 

    RETURN head

END PROCEDURE

AFTER DELETION: HEAD → [102, "Bob"] → NULL
sq.QUESTION_DESC:
Consider an company is maintaining a singly linked list of employee records in an HR management system. Each node in the list contains an employee's ID, name, and a pointer to the next employee.

Currently, the list has the following employees (in order): [101, "Alice"] → [102, "Bob"] → [103, "Charlie"] → NULL.

As part of the operations:

  1. Delete the first employee from the list.
  2. Then, delete the last employee from the updated list.

Write pseudocode for both operations and show the resulting list after each deletion.

lq.ANSWER:
#include <stdio.h>

#include <stdlib.h>

 

// Node structure representing each song

struct Song {

    int songID; // You can replace this with a string if needed

    struct Song* next;

};

 

// Function to delete the last song in the playlist

void deleteLastSong(struct Song** head) {

    if (*head == NULL) {

        printf("Playlist is empty. No song to delete.\n");

        return;

    }

 

    // If there is only one song in the playlist

    if ((*head)->next == NULL) {

        printf("Deleted last song with ID: %d\n", (*head)->songID);

        free(*head);

        *head = NULL;

        return;

    }

 

    // Traverse to the second-last song

    struct Song* temp = *head;

    while (temp->next->next != NULL) {

        temp = temp->next;

    }

 

    printf("Deleted last song with ID: %d\n", temp->next->songID);

    free(temp->next);

    temp->next = NULL;

}

 

// Utility: Add song at the end (for demo/testing)

void addSong(struct Song** head, int songID) {

    struct Song* newSong = (struct Song*)malloc(sizeof(struct Song));

    newSong->songID = songID;

    newSong->next = NULL;

 

    if (*head == NULL) {

        *head = newSong;

        return;

    }

 

    struct Song* temp = *head;

    while (temp->next != NULL) {

        temp = temp->next;

    }

    temp->next = newSong;

}

 

// Utility: Print playlist

void printPlaylist(struct Song* head) {

    if (head == NULL) {

        printf("Playlist is empty.\n");

        return;

    }

 

    printf("Playlist: ");

    while (head != NULL) {

        printf("%d -> ", head->songID);

        head = head->next;

    }

    printf("NULL\n");

}

 

// Driver code

int main() {

    struct Song* playlist = NULL;

 

    addSong(&playlist, 101);

    addSong(&playlist, 102);

    addSong(&playlist, 103);

 

    printPlaylist(playlist);          // Playlist: 101 -> 102 -> 103 -> NULL

    deleteLastSong(&playlist);        // Deletes 103

    printPlaylist(playlist);          // Playlist: 101 -> 102 -> NULL

 

    deleteLastSong(&playlist);        // Deletes 102

    deleteLastSong(&playlist);        // Deletes 101

    deleteLastSong(&playlist);        // Playlist is empty

 

    return 0;

}
